comments.body:
FIX + VERIFICATION (Gerrit change 1678).

Mechanism reconfirmed against current main. `tests/conftest.py` already defaults `REBAR_ROOT`
to a sandbox repo for every test (bug dd62), and its docstring notes that a test which
`delenv`s it escapes that default. This test does exactly that, deliberately, because the
depth-fallback resolution is what it pins — so `main()` runs against the REAL checkout.
`_pause_exit_code` runs BEFORE `_post_pause_preflight`, and `read_pause` was the one advisory
call left unstubbed, so a corrupt (or merely present) `refs/reconciler/gate` in the runner's
checkout returned early and `check_pass_lock` was never called.

AC1: `read_pause` is now stubbed alongside the others through a shared helper
(`_stub_main_advisory`) that both tests use, so the stub set cannot drift between them.
`REBAR_ROOT` stays cleared and the resolution assertion is unchanged; the test additionally
asserts `read_pause` received the SAME resolved root, which pins resolution at the FIRST
advisory call — the one that used to reach the real refs.

AC2: `test_main_resolves_repo_root_even_when_the_ambient_gate_ref_is_corrupt` injects the
corruption one layer BELOW the stub, patching `_advisory_lock._load_ref_lock` to return a
ref-lock whose `read_pause` raises `RefLockCorruptError` — the exact error the advisory layer
converts into `ReconcileGateError`. It then asserts the resolution assertions still hold AND
that the corrupt layer was never reached. RED verified by removing only the `read_pause`
stub:

- the regression test fails with "a corrupt ambient refs/reconciler/gate must not stop main()
  reaching the preflight"
- the original test fails with "read_pause must be called before the preflight"

Restoring the stub returns both to green, so the guard is not bought by going blind.

AC3 audit: widened beyond the file. Eleven test files clear `REBAR_ROOT`, but this is the
ONLY one that also enters the advisory/gate path — the single other grep hit is an unrelated
`"advisory": []` JSON key in `test_reviewbot_ensure_tickets.py`. Within the file there are no
sibling tests to convert: exactly one test clears `REBAR_ROOT`, and the only other
`read_pause` reference already patches it. Nothing further to change.

AC4: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass; the file passes (14 passed) and the reconciler
unit tree passes (2409 passed).

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_main.py::test_main_without_repo_root_passes_resolved_repo_root`
failed CI (`AssertionError: check_pass_lock must be called when main() runs`), costing
Gerrit change 1658 a spurious `Verified -1` in a file that change does not touch.

## Mechanism (confirmed against current main)

The suite already isolates every test from the enclosing checkout: an autouse fixture in
`tests/conftest.py` (lines 268-281, bug dd62) defaults `REBAR_ROOT` to a sandbox repo, and
its own docstring notes that a test which `delenv`s it escapes that default.

This test does exactly that (line 530) — deliberately, because the genuine depth-fallback
`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]` is the thing under test. So `main()` runs against the
REAL repository root. It patches `check_pass_lock`, `check_phase_gate`, `acquire_pass_lock`
and `release_pass_lock`, but NOT `read_pause`.

In `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py`, `_pause_exit_code` (line 160) runs
BEFORE `_post_pause_preflight` (line 189), which is what calls `check_pass_lock`.
`_pause_exit_code` calls `advisory.read_pause(repo_root)`, which raises `ReconcileGateError`
on a corrupt gate ref (`_advisory_lock.py:232-238`) and returns early. So when the runner's
checkout carries a corrupt or leftover `refs/reconciler/gate`, `main()` returns before
`check_pass_lock` and the assertion fails through no fault of the code under test. The job
log carries exactly that path's message. A merely PRESENT (uncorrupt) pause marker derails
it the same way, via the PAUSED branch.

The defect is the unmocked `read_pause`: a unit test's outcome must not depend on the
ambient refs of whatever checkout it happens to run in.

## Fix

Stub `read_pause` alongside the advisory calls already stubbed, so ambient gate state cannot
reach `main()`, while `REBAR_ROOT` stays cleared and the repo-root RESOLUTION assertion the
test exists for is preserved unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The test no longer depends on the enclosing repo's `refs/reconciler/gate`:
      `read_pause` is stubbed, and the existing assertion that the resolved root contains
      `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` still holds. The test additionally
      asserts the stubbed `read_pause` was called with that same resolved root, so the
      resolution path stays pinned at the FIRST advisory call rather than only the later one.
- [ ] AC2 — A regression test simulates the corrupt ambient gate ref at the layer below the
      stub (`_ref_lock.read_pause` raising `RefLockCorruptError`) and asserts the resolution
      assertions still hold. Verified RED against the pre-fix test body, which fails with the
      exact CI message, and GREEN after.
- [ ] AC3 — Audit of the file for sibling tests that clear `REBAR_ROOT` and leave an advisory
      call unmocked; the result is stated in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] AC4 — `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the affected file pass.
compiled_state.title: Reconciler main test reads real repo gate ref; corrupt ref flakes CI
